Create and add a stencil to pain drawings.

Source: R/pdr_add_stencil.R
pdr_add_stencil.Rd

Users should only add a stencil to pain drawings that are intended to serve as stencils for other pain drawings. To apply stencils see pdr_modify_rgba().

Usage

pdr_add_stencil(pdr_list, threshold = 1, channel = "A", by = "<")

Arguments

pdr_list

A pdr_list in which every pdr_drawing has an .rgba element (see pdr_add_rgba() and pdr_match()).

threshold

A threshold value which determines a pixel as being 0 or 1

channel

A string specifying which channels of the RGBA matrix to compare to the threshold.

by

Either '<' or '>'

Value

A pdr_list (see pdr_match()) where each pdr_drawing has two added elements: .stencil, a numeric matrix of dimensions height x width with values 0 or 1, and .stencil_inverted, the same matrix with 0 and 1 swapped.

Details

Pain drawings can be used as stencils and applied to other pain drawings. This is typically useful, when a particular region of a pain drawing is of particular interest. E.g. when only a specific anatomical regions of the pain drawing is relevant.

This function reduces a pain drawing to a stencil – ie. the RGBA data is reduced to a single level (alpha) with just 0 and 1 values.

The 'threshold' parameter determines the threshold at which a pixel's value is dichotomized to 0 or 1 (FALSE or TRUE) as per the 'by' parameter. E.g. a pixel with alpha value 0.4 will evaluate to 0 by '>' a 'threshold' of 0.5. With the defaults (threshold = 1, by = "<", channel = "A") a pixel is set to 1 when its alpha is below 1, i.e. when it is not fully opaque. For a drawing rendered with pdr_add_rgba(), this is the transparent (undrawn) area, while fully opaque (drawn) pixels become 0. The inverse is stored in .stencil_inverted.

The 'channel' parameter determines which of the R, G, B and A channels should be evaluated in reference to the threshold. E.g. 'RGBA' evaluates all of the channels by 'OR', and 'A' evaluates only the alpha channel.

See also

pdr_modify_rgba(), pdr_plot_stencil()

Examples

# \donttest{
pdr_example_data[1:3, ] |>
  dplyr::mutate(pdr_data = pdr_add_rgba(pdr_data, polygon = "both")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pdr_data = pdr_add_stencil(pdr_data, threshold = 0.5, channel = "A", by = "<"))
#> # A tibble: 3 × 6
